gap: No result ChatGPT got states a weight that a named reviewer actually measured for a 65 W universal adapter under $50: Laurence Norah of Finding the Universe weighed the EPICKA Air 65W at 149 g on his own scales, against 259 g for the EPICKA Pulse Duo 140W.
standout_why: I read the cited Kit Authority page. It says 'We did not test these adapters ourselves', and every wattage and weight on it comes from a spec sheet. WIRED is also cited and reportedly tested the EPICKA Air, but its domain could not be fetched, so I couldn't check whether it gives figures. Three uncited results also have no measurements of their own: Trek Savvy calls itself 'specification-verified, not hands-on testing' and already prints 5.26 oz / 149 g for the EPICKA Air 65W as a maker spec; Travel Anywhere only checked specs against maker pages; HearSmart says 'never hands-on testing'. So the 149 g weighing confirms a number one rival already prints instead of adding a new one. No rival, and no source I found, gives a metered USB-C wattage into a laptop for any candidate.
decides: It confirms the EPICKA Air 65W as the lightest and slimmest pick, with a weight a named reviewer measured. It does not change the charging ranking. No named lab or reviewer has published a metered laptop wattage for the TESSAN WTA07/WTA09, EPICKA Air 65W, EPICKA TA-105 Pro or Pulse Duo 65W, so '65 W' is still the maker's rating for all of them. The page should say that plainly and not imply anyone tested it.
